title: Wild Man Training (Hypertrophy Log #0)
summary: While camping, NH trains with a log, an axe, gymnastic rings, a band, a loop, a wooden handle and three 10 lb plates. He runs two days of giant sets that pre-fatigue muscles to reach failure with light loads. He ends with a physique update at 215 lb and six feet after six months of bulking, saying he plans to keep bulking for years.
claims: With limited equipment, superset movements that hit the same muscle so you reach failure with light weight; not optimal, but it works away from the gym
Gymnastic rings are invaluable for anyone without a home gym
A wooden stick in a band loop makes a better pushdown handle than any V-bar, removing grip demand; he kept it for his home gym
Rings are his favourite way to do chin-ups because the wrists can rotate freely
Chin-ups train the brachioradialis, so doing them before forearm work pre-fatigues it; in a normal gym, do forearm isolation fresh
Occasionally train biceps in the lengthened position for injury prevention
Knee raises should curl the pelvis up at the top and let the legs stretch the abs at the bottom; done properly you can't do many
Close-hand push-ups with fingers forward hammer the triceps long and lateral heads, with failure in the triceps rather than chest or shoulders
Shoulders are his weak point; with a huge upper back and traps, small delts look ridiculous, so they must catch up
Each wild-man session took 25 minutes max of pure giant sets
Choose the leverage that makes the muscle work hardest, not the one that makes you strongest
He does rear-delt rows bringing forearm to biceps without flaring the elbow, emphasising the bottom stretch; normally 45-50 lb in the gym
Axe ulnar deviation trains the brachioradialis and resistance is adjusted by hand position, but it can't be progressively overloaded, so reverse curls are better
Treat tendinitis by sending blood to the tendon and strengthening the weak muscle with isolation, not by just resting; his elbow tendinitis came from excessive close-grip bench volume
He has 18-inch natural arms despite poor arm genetics, from serious arm isolation
After six months of bulking he is 215 lb at six feet; arms and upper back grew while the waist barely increased and abs stay visible
He doesn't care about cutting and may stay on a small-surplus, performance-focused bulk for two to three more years
exercises: palms on the stick, no thumb wrap
limited ROM hammer curl, no full supination, pronate at top
rotate pelvis up, stretch at bottom
loop around wrist, fist up, hold ring for angle
engage upper back first, start from negative
forearm to biceps, elbow not flared, stretch at bottom
rear delts without aggravating the shoulder
hand closer to head makes it easier
